title: Print subarray with maximum subarray sum (extended version of above problem)
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Return the actual subarray achieving the maximum sum, not just the value.
intuition: Kadane already knows when a new subarray begins — it is precisely the moment cur restarts at a[i]. Record that index and close the interval whenever best improves.

approaches.title: Optimal: Kadane with start/end bookkeeping
approaches.idea: tentative start moves on restart; commit start/end when best updates.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4]
restart at i=1 (tentative=1), i=3 (tentative=3)
best becomes 6 at i=6 -> start=3 end=6 -> [4,-1,2,1]
approaches.whyWorks: A restart is the only place a new optimal subarray can begin.

edgeCases: Ties — which subarray do you return?
commonMistakes: Updating start at every restart instead of only when best improves
Returning indices from a run that was later beaten
patternRecognition: "Reconstruct the witness" -> store the decision point, not the whole history
followUps: Return the shortest such subarray on ties
Maximum sum rectangle in a 2-D matrix
interviewInsight: Reconstruction questions are really about DP traceback discipline; the tentative/committed split is the whole trick.
